column1: # QUALIFIABLE FIXTURE QUEUE -- never-evaluated cells whose fixture is PROVEN able to express failure via exit status.
# Produced 2026-08-15 by hermit-bytes. Source of truth read at origin/main 61b9ba7aa (cells.json + tests/e2e/manifests/*.toml).
# THIS LIST IS A FLOOR, NOT THE POPULATION. Do not plan as if it were complete.
#   83 of 283 screened C programs are CONFIRMED qualifiable. Measured screen sensitivity 14/26 = 0.54, exact 95% CI [0.33, 0.73].
#   The true qualifiable count is therefore probably between roughly 117 and 259 of the 283. NO POINT ESTIMATE IS SUPPORTED and none is given.
# UNIT, BECAUSE TWO COUNTS ARE IN PLAY AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE:
#   83 is a count of PROGRAMS. Exit-gating is a property of the program, not of a cell.
#   Those 83 programs carry 380 never-evaluated CELLS (test x mode x backend), which is what this file lists and what a lane agent acts on.
#   PER-BACKEND COUNTS BELOW SUM TO 380, NOT TO 83.
# DO NOT EXPECT ONE MORE MUTATION FAMILY TO CLOSE THE GAP. Of the 13 calibration misses, 10 were 'no mutation pattern matched',
#   and those 10 are spread across FOUR manifest categories (backend-parity-c, c-programs, determinism-stress-c, system-utils)
#   rather than clustering in one. That is evidence against a single missing family and for several.
# WHAT 'qualifiable' MEANS HERE: a semantic mutation of the fixture changed its EXIT STATUS, with both binaries built and run and their
#   exit and output compared. It means the fixture CAN express failure in the channel the verdict keys on. IT IS NOT a claim that the cell
#   passes, that the backend can run it, or that it is ready to enable. Backend capability is a separate and independent gate.
# A GUARD WITH ZERO HITS THAT IS NOT DEAD WEIGHT: a mutant that dies by SIGNAL is recorded NOT-DETERMINABLE and never qualifiable,
#   because a crash induced by the mutation is not the fixture expressing failure. It fired 0 times across every run.
#   THE ZERO IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN ABSENCE: the guard was in place BEFORE any count was taken, not added afterwards.
# RESIDUAL OF THE 283-PROGRAM SCREEN, SHOWN RATHER THAN DISTRIBUTED: 105 no mutation pattern matched | 6 mutation applied but no observable
#   change | 2 build failed | 1 timeout. The 105 are the instrument, not the fixtures, and must not be read as 'probably not qualifiable'.
#   backend-parity-c/eventfd-semantics and backend-parity-c/vectored-io are APPLIED-BUT-INERT, not unscreened: the mutation fired and the
#   program behaved identically. Different defect, different remedy. NOT FIXED AND NOT CLAIMED.
# CALIBRATION: 38 points, 27 known exit-gated and 11 known cannot-fail, from hermit-sabre's exit-gating screen (external) plus 10
#   hand-established verdicts. ZERO calibration points were drawn from the screen being measured. False positives: 0 of 11, re-checked
#   after every widening. One source conflict is on record: backend-parity-c/eventfd-semantics is CANNOT_FAIL in sabre's screen and
#   exit-gated by hand; sensitivity is reported both ways (0.52 including it, 0.54 excluding it).
# NOT SCREENED AND OUTSIDE EVERY COUNT ABOVE: 42 shell programs and 1 Rust program behind the same never-evaluated population.
# PER-BACKEND CELLS: dbt=47  kvm=71  liteinst=79  native=73  ptrace=81  sabre=29   TOTAL=380
# PER-MODE CELLS:    naked=73  replay=81  verify=226   TOTAL=380
# ================ CAVEAT ADDED 2026-08-15 AFTER SHIPPING: THIS QUEUE IS SCOPED TO THE EXIT-STATUS CHANNEL ================
# VERIFY ALSO REFUSES ON STDOUT DIVERGENCE AT IDENTICAL EXIT STATUS. Replicated on this host, both directions, with a control:
#   control arm  -- identical stdout, exit 0            -> verdict=matched,  bitwise_parity=true
#   test arm     -- DIFFERING stdout, SAME exit 0       -> verdict=diverged, bitwise_parity=false, guest_exit_code=0,
#                                                          literal harness line: "Mismatch in stdout between run 1 and run 2"
#   The test arm is only meaningful because the divergence was PROVEN: a first attempt used a counter file under /tmp and
#   PASSED VACUOUSLY -- the container gives the guest a private /tmp, the guest's writes never reached the host, and both runs
#   printed the same line. Moving the counter under the repo made the runs share it; the state file read 2 afterwards, which is
#   the proof that stdout actually differed. A "matched" verdict from the /tmp version would have been evidence of nothing.
#   This is REPLICATION of a devbig014 finding on the same codebase, not independent corroboration: it shows the behaviour is
#   not host-specific and nothing more. n=1 per direction, one guest, one mechanism.
# CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS FILE: THE 83 / 380 ROWS BELOW ARE CORRECT BUT SCOPED. They are the cells whose fixture discriminates via
#   EXIT STATUS. They are NOT the complete set of refusable cells, because a fixture that always exits 0 can still discriminate
#   via stdout, and the harness refuses on that.
# CONSEQUENCE FOR THE OTHER BUCKETS: "cannot-fail" IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE EXIT CHANNEL ONLY AND IS THE WRONG LABEL FOR VERIFY
#   PURPOSES. In the same screen, 58 of the 283 programs had a mutation that MOVED STDOUT WHILE EXIT STAYED 0 -- 29 currently
#   labelled not-exit-gated and 29 labelled cannot-fail. Those 58 are candidates for stdout-channel refusability, so a combined
#   floor across both channels would be on the order of 141 of 283 rather than 83.
# WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS: verify compares two runs of the SAME binary, whereas the screen compared
#   an ORIGINAL against a MUTANT. Showing a mutation moves a fixture's stdout proves its stdout is sensitive to program
#   behaviour; it does NOT prove that a real backend defect would move it. So 141 IS NOT A SECOND FLOOR -- the 58 are candidates
#   needing their own screen against the stdout channel, and that screen has not been run.
# ======= FOLLOW-UP 2026-08-15: THE 58 STDOUT-CHANNEL CANDIDATES REMAIN UNSCREENED, AND THIS IS A STRUCTURAL LIMIT =======
# The caveat above sized 58 programs that moved stdout while exit stayed 0. THEY HAVE NOT BEEN SCREENED AND THE COMBINED
# FIGURE ON THE ORDER OF 141 IS STILL NOT A FLOOR. The reason is worth recording because it will not change by trying harder.
# WHAT A FAITHFUL STIMULUS WOULD HAVE TO BE: verify compares TWO RUNS OF THE SAME BINARY, so the perturbation must be applied
#   to the DETERMINIZATION, not to the source. A source mutation shows a fixture's stdout is sensitive to program behaviour;
#   it does not model what verify sees. The right stimulus is a relaxation that makes the backend fail to determinize something,
#   after which a discriminating fixture's stdout should differ between the two runs.
# SUCH RELAXATIONS EXIST AS FLAGS, AND EVERY ONE TESTED FAILED ONE OF THE TWO REQUIREMENTS -- keep the run alive, and be able to
#     --no-virtualize-time (+ --no-virtualize-metadata, which it requires): on a clock_gettime-printing guest the run ERRORS,
#         "Sandbox container exited unexpectedly / Exited(1)". That is a broken run, not a divergence.
#     --no-rcb-time, --no-virtualize-metadata, --chaos: the run stays alive and the constant-output control stays matched, but
#         NONE of them moved stdout even for that maximally time-sensitive guest. verdict=matched in all three.
#     --no-deterministic-io, --no-sequentialize-threads: rejected by the CLI for this subcommand.
# LIMIT OF THE CHAOS PROBE, STATED SO IT IS NOT OVERREAD: the racy guest used to probe --chaos (tests/chaos/thread_interleaving.c)
#   printed IDENTICALLY ACROSS TWO NATIVE RUNS, so it was never a valid probe for a scheduling stimulus. --chaos IS NOT REFUTED;
#   it is untested against a guest whose output genuinely varies with scheduling.
# STIMULUS VALIDATION DISCIPLINE USED THROUGHOUT: a stimulus counts only if the NEGATIVE CONTROL (a constant-output guest) stays
#   matched under it. Two candidates were discarded on that ground alone.
# THE DETERMINATE FINDING: NO FAITHFUL SINGLE-BACKEND STDOUT-CHANNEL STIMULUS WAS FOUND. Screening the 58 requires either a
#   second backend to compare against, or a guest-level probe proven to diverge natively through a mechanism Hermit is supposed
#   to determinize and then used to validate a relaxation. The stdout channel is verify's comparison of two runs, and a
#   single-backend screen has only one run to work with -- which is the structural reason, not a gap in effort.
# ==== CORRECTION 2026-08-15: THERE IS ONE CHANNEL, NOT TWO, AND IT IS HERMIT'S EXIT STATUS -- NOT THE GUEST'S ====
# Verified from source at hermit-cli/src/bin/hermit/verify.rs:415, into_exit_status:
#     Verdict::Matched  -> Ok(self.guest_status)      hermit's exit becomes THE GUEST'S status
#     Verdict::Diverged -> Err("Mismatch between run 1 and run 2 outputs.")   hermit exits NON-ZERO regardless of the guest
# So the stdout comparison happens INSIDE hermit and surfaces as HERMIT'S exit status. IT IS NOT A SEPARATE STDOUT CHANNEL,
# and the "58 stdout-channel candidates" framing in the block below is superseded: those cells reach hermit's exit THROUGH
# stdout. Same single channel. (Finding relayed from hermit-revents and re-derived here from the source, not inherited.)
# WHAT THIS SCREEN ACTUALLY OBSERVED, STATED UNAMBIGUOUSLY BECAUSE THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT:
#   THIS SCREEN OBSERVES THE GUEST'S EXIT STATUS. It compiles each fixture and runs the BINARY DIRECTLY, with no hermit in
#   the loop at all. Every "exit 0->1" in the evidence column below is a GUEST exit transition.
#   The 83 rows remain CORRECT: a guest exit transition does reach hermit's exit, because Matched returns guest_status.
#   BUT "cannot-fail" IS DEFINITIVELY THE WRONG LABEL. It means only "the GUEST always exits 0". A fixture that always exits 0
#   can still be perfectly refusable, because a divergence between the two runs makes HERMIT exit non-zero irrespective of it.
# AND THE REFRAME DOES NOT MAKE THE 58 CHEAP TO SCREEN -- THE STRUCTURAL LIMIT BELOW STILL STANDS. Switching the screen to
#   observe hermit's exit does not resolve them: under `hermit run --verify` a MUTATED fixture produces the same wrong output
#   in BOTH runs, so the verdict is still Matched and hermit still exits 0. Making hermit's exit move requires the two runs to
#   genuinely differ, which requires a real nondeterminism source -- exactly the stimulus that could not be induced.
#   The correction fixes the MECHANISM and the LABEL. It does not supply the missing stimulus.
# BOUND CARRIED FROM THE SOURCE OF THE FINDING, SO IT IS NOT OVERREAD: the evidence that hermit refuses a stdout divergence is
#   HERMIT-LEVEL. The counter guest was not run through the harness as a cell. "hermit refuses it" is established;
#   "the harness books it as a red cell" is established for replay only. THE FIRST MUST NOT BORROW THE SECOND'S STRENGTH.
# ===== CORRECTION 2026-08-15: THE POPULATION NOW RECONCILES. 86 PROGRAMS WERE NEVER NAMED IN THIS HEADER. =====
# Found by hermit-teardown, and the defect was REPRODUCIBILITY, not soundness: a reader who added up the published
# numbers got 83 + 105 + 6 + 2 + 1 = 197 of 283 and had to conclude the file was wrong. The queue was substantially
# sound the whole time; the header simply never stated two of the four buckets. That is the harmful version, because
# it costs a careful reader their confidence.
# THE COMPLETE SCREEN OF 283 C PROGRAMS, ALL FOUR BUCKETS, SUMMING TO 283:
#     qualifiable (exit-gated)     83      <- the 380 rows below are these programs' cells
#     not-exit-gated               29      <- NOT previously stated in this header
#     cannot-fail                  57      <- NOT previously stated in this header
#     NOT-DETERMINABLE            114      = 105 no mutation pattern matched + 6 mutation applied but no observable
#                                             change + 2 build failed (original) + 1 mutant timed out
# THE 86 THAT WERE MISSING ARE 29 not-exit-gated + 57 cannot-fail.
# AND THE 58 IS A CROSS-CUT, NOT A BUCKET -- WHICH IS WHY ADDING IT TO THE OTHERS DOES NOT WORK. The 58 named in the
# caveat above are the programs whose mutation MOVED OUTPUT WHILE EXIT STAYED 0. They span two buckets:
#     29 of them are the entire not-exit-gated bucket
#     the remaining 28 cannot-fail programs are a different case: no mutation pattern matched AND main cannot
#        terminate non-zero, so no output movement was observed for them at all
#     29 + 29 + 28 = 86.  DO NOT ADD 58 TO A BUCKET TOTAL; IT OVERLAPS TWO OF THEM.
# hermit-teardown's reading -- that the 86 were presumably not-exit-gated, leaving 28 unaccounted -- arrived at a real
# number by a slightly different route: the 28 is genuine, but the 86 is not one bucket.
# A METHOD POINT FROM THE SAME REVIEW, KEPT BECAUSE IT GENERALISES: GRADE YOUR ZEROS, DO NOT REPORT THEM FLAT.
#     WEAK zero: "no rows lacking 'exit' in evidence: 0" -- the evidence vocabulary is five strings and ALL FIVE
#        contain "exit", so that zero could not have come out any other way. It confirms nothing.
#     STRONG zeros: "deleted lines: 0", which enumerates diff lines directly, and "unmatched: 0 of 380",
#   A zero is only evidence if the measurement could have produced a non-zero.
# REVIEWER INDEPENDENCE, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THE NEXT PERSON ASKING FOR A CHECK NEEDS IT: hermit-teardown has now
# TOUCHED backend-parity-c/eventfd-semantics and backend-parity-c/vectored-io -- the two rows named applied-but-inert
# above, and the subject of its PR #2282. IT DISQUALIFIED ITSELF, UNPROMPTED, FROM FUTURE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF THOSE
# TWO ROWS. It remains independent for the rest of the queue. None of the defects it found was bar-lowering.
